events.title: Hollywood Sign Dedicated
events.description: The original 'HOLLYWOODLAND' sign was dedicated in the Hollywood Hills of Los Angeles as an advertisement for a real estate development. It was later shortened to 'HOLLYWOOD' in 1949.
events.significance: The sign became one of the most recognizable landmarks in the world and a lasting symbol of the American film industry.

events.title: Live Aid Concerts Held
events.description: Live Aid, a dual-venue benefit concert held at Wembley Stadium in London and John F. Kennedy Stadium in Philadelphia, was broadcast to an estimated 1.9 billion viewers across about 150 countries. It was organized by Bob Geldof and Midge Ure to raise funds for famine relief in Ethiopia.
events.significance: It was a landmark in global charity fundraising and in live television broadcasting, raising tens of millions of dollars and drawing worldwide attention to the Ethiopian famine.

events.title: Treaty of Berlin Signed
events.description: The Congress of Berlin concluded with the signing of the Treaty of Berlin, which revised the Treaty of San Stefano after the Russo-Turkish War. Held under the chairmanship of Otto von Bismarck, it redrew borders in the Balkans and recognized the independence of Romania, Serbia, and Montenegro.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped the Balkans and the balance of power in Europe, leaving tensions that contributed to the instability preceding World War I.

events.title: Assassination of Jean-Paul Marat
events.description: Radical journalist and French Revolution leader Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed to death in his bath by Charlotte Corday, a Girondin sympathizer, in Paris.
events.significance: His death turned him into a martyr of the Revolution and was used to justify intensification of the Reign of Terror. The scene was immortalized in Jacques-Louis David's painting 'The Death of Marat'.

events.title: New York City Draft Riots Begin
events.description: Violent unrest broke out in New York City in protest of the Union's new conscription law during the American Civil War. The riots lasted several days, and mobs targeted Black residents, abolitionists, and government buildings.
events.significance: They were among the largest civil insurrections in American history, other than the Civil War itself, and revealed deep class and racial tensions in the North.
